To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
manure-application mode and rainfall intensity and time are important factors affecting algal yields.
the algal-gross-potential test is a sensitive tool to assess the effects of agricultural practices upon the quality of agricultural run-off water.

the algal growth potential test (AGPT), which is a simple and sensitive method, can be used to assess the effect of manure-application rate, mode, and rainfall characteristics upon runoff water quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of manure application on the quality of runoff water and the algal growth potential of runoff water.
the assessment of the effects of manure application on runoff quality and the potential toxicity of agricultural runoff water to aquatic life.
the assessment of the effects of the manure-application rate, mode and rainfall characteristics on runoff-water quality and the effects of runoff dilution on algal growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

manure application to soil can stimulate the algal growth in runoff water, but the extent of the stimulation is dependent on the mode of manure-application, the manure-application rate to soil, the characteristics of rainfall, and the degree of dilution.
the algal growth potential of runoff water is dependent on the mode and rate of manure application to soil and on the rainfall characteristics.
the surface manure application mode, high manure application rate, high rainfall intensity and long rainfall time, and low dilution of runoff can increase the algal growth in runoff water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the algal assay can be an appropriate method to monitor the quality of agricultural surface runoff water and that the AGPT is more sensitive than chemical analyses for the assessment of the effects of manure application on the quality of runoff.
, in general, the algal growth is positively correlated with the nutrient load from manure application and rainfall.
the surface mode of application and a high manure-application rate are not recommended for manure management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the algal growth test is a sensitive and reliable method to assess the water-quality impacts of agricultural runoff.

algal assays and the chemical analyses of runoff are complementary in that the algal assays can provide an indication of the toxicity of runoff water and the chemical analyses can provide an indication on the nutrient load of runoff water.
the algal growth in runoff from manure-amended soils can be limited by the availability of N and P.
